subject: sleeping koala
title: The 5 Animals That Sleep the Most, Ranked (The Sloth Doesn't Make the List)

scenes.text: The five sleepiest animals, ranked. The sloth is not on the list, and number one barely wakes up.

scenes.label: Python · 18 hours
scenes.text: Number five: the python. Around 18 hours a day, and after a big meal it lies still for days.

scenes.label: Giant armadillo · 18.1 h
scenes.text: Number four: the giant armadillo. About 18.1 hours, almost all of it underground in burrows it digs itself.

scenes.label: Opossum · 18–19 hours
scenes.text: Number three: the North American opossum. Around 18 to 19 hours a day, playing dead the rest of the time.

scenes.label: Brown bat · 19.9 hours
scenes.text: Number two: the little brown bat. 19.9 hours a day, hanging upside down, awake only long enough to hunt.

scenes.label: Koala · up to 22 hours
scenes.text: Number one: the koala. 18 to 22 hours a day. Eucalyptus leaves give so little energy that staying awake is a luxury.

description:
The five animals that sleep the most hours per day, ranked.
Pythons sleep about 18 hours a day, giant armadillos about 18.1, North American opossums roughly 18 to 19, and little brown bats 19.9, according to sleep-lab data compiled by neuroscientists at the University of Washington from studies by Jerome Siegel and others. Koalas sleep 18 to 22 hours a day because their eucalyptus diet is so low in nutrients and slow to digest. Sloths are left off: the old 20-hour figure came from captive animals, and wild sloths sleep far less.
Which of these would you trade places with?
first_comment: Wild sloths fitted with tiny brain recorders in Panama slept only about 9.6 hours a day, so the famous 20-hour sloth was a zoo animal with nothing to do. Which would you have put at number one? And what should we rank next: the animals that sleep the least?
